description: Catena org-wide Renovate policy. Extend it from any catenahq repo with: extends: github>catenahq/renovate-config. It layers Catena operational config (PR limits, timezone, labels, lockfile cadence, automerge) on top of the generic security baseline github>catenahq/scanctl:secure-base, which owns the 7-day adoption cooldown, GitHub Actions SHA-pinning, and CVE fast-track. Public on purpose: it carries no secrets, so every consumer (public repos included) resolves it cleanly and the policy stays transparent. The self-hosted runner lives separately in the private catenahq/renovate repo.

No top-level schedule: timing is controlled solely by the single self-hosted Renovate cron (catenahq/renovate, every 4 hours). A Renovate-internal schedule (e.g. before 5am) silently no-ops every run that lands outside the window -- a delayed scheduled run OR any manual workflow_dispatch -- so the same invocation behaves differently by wall clock. Without one, every run, scheduled or manual, does identical work. The 7-day minimumReleaseAge cooldown from secure-base still throttles churn; lockFileMaintenance keeps its own daily window below.

Every update automerges once all its checks pass: CI on the pull request is the gate, and the release bench, the app tests or the deploy that follow the merge carry the proof that it works. No rule here holds a PR for a human.

platformAutomerge is off: Renovate merges an automerge PR itself, on a run after the one that opened it, and only once every check on the PR has passed. GitHub's native auto-merge waits only for the checks a branch ruleset requires, so in a repo without one it merges the PR before CI reports. Renovate counts its own aged-release check as passing (secure-base internalChecksAsSuccess), so the gate is each repo's CI running on pull_request: a repo whose PRs get no CI check would automerge unchecked.

A `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...` comment above a `*_VERSION` line is tracked in workflow and action files (customManagers:githubActionsVersions) and in Dockerfiles as an ARG or ENV (customManagers:dockerfileVersions), so a tool pinned in a run: block or a build stage is bumped like any other dependency.

lockFileMaintenance is exempt from the cooldown (secure-base). A relock re-resolves every dependency inside its existing declared range, which is how most transitive-only CVE fixes reach the lockfile without a direct-dependency bump, so an unmerged relock withholds exactly those. It automerges safely because it changes no declared range and every check on the PR -- including the scanctl diff gate, which fails on any CVE the PR INTRODUCES -- has to pass first.

lockFileMaintenance runs daily, in the window 00:00-03:59 America/Toronto, which one 4-hourly run lands in each day. For a transitive-only fix the relock is the only path: Renovate's vulnerability PRs refuse a change to package-lock.json alone unless lockfileVersion is 1. A run outside the window does no relock; the Dependency Dashboard checkbox starts one at once.

Renovate writes npm lock files with npm 11 (constraints.npm, read before any version a repo's package.json names). npm 12 refuses the registry tarball of any package with bundleDependencies when it writes a lock file (npm/cli#9800, open), which fails the artifact update of every pull request in a repo whose lock holds one, such as @tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi.

packageRules.description: GitHub Actions minor and patch bumps: one group.
Container image and compose bumps: one group.

First-party actions/reusable workflows ride their branch ref (e.g. catenahq/scanctl github-reusable.yml@main): do NOT pin them to a SHA. secure-base SHA-pins third-party actions because their tags are mutable supply-chain surface, but our own repos are trusted, ruleset-gated, and the zizmor policy explicitly allows catenahq/* ref-pins. Pinning them would freeze every caller at a stale SHA (secure-base disables same-tag digest updates) and force a manual per-repo bump on every scanctl change.
